polymers with antibacterial properties, or modified to confer such activity, can be used to develop polymeric nanoparticles as antibacterial drugs delivery systems.
polymer‐based nanoparticles can be considered as promising drug delivery systems to increase the efficacy and reduce the toxicity of available antibiotic agents.
the use of polymeric nanoparticles as devices for antibacterially active drugs can be an effective approach to increase their therapeutic efficacy and reduce the risk of resistance development.

the design and the development of polymeric nanoparticle constructs able to deliver antibiotics and/or to display antibacterial activity.
the development of polymeric nanoparticles as drug delivery system for the treatment of bacterial infections.
the development and application of polymeric nanoparticles as devices for antibacterially active drugs.

the exploitation of nanotechnology represents a valid strategy to improve the efficacy of current antibiotic therapies.
the development of polymeric nanoparticles for antibacterial therapies could be an interesting and promising strategy for overcoming the antibiotic resistance.
polymeric nanoparticle constructs are promising devices for antibacterial treatment, able to improve the efficacy of the conventional antibiotic therapy.

we have developed a novel approach for the design of polymer‐based nanosized systems able to act as antibacterial devices for antibiotic therapy.

we have been exploring the use of polymer‐based nanocarriers for antibacterial therapy, with a particular interest for the use of polymers with antibacterial properties or modified to confer them with bactericidal power.

polymer‐based nanoparticles can be used as drug delivery systems, to increase the antibacterial efficacy of the conventional antibiotic therapies.
